title: THR sieve/riddle revival — can Doubt preserve revival vs transmission?
question: Does the checked public evidence establish that the revival of UK sieve and riddle making preserved and transmitted the older tacit skill completely?
verdict: No. Public sources establish a reported revival and one reported direct-learning route, but they do not establish what tacit knowledge was transmitted, reconstructed, adapted, or newly learned.

nodes.label: Current position
nodes.text: The bounded record supports revival and partial learning-lineage claims, not complete tacit-skill transmission.

nodes.label: Reported revival
nodes.text: Heritage Crafts reports extinction in 2017 followed by revival by two new makers by March 2019.

nodes.label: Reported direct-learning route
nodes.text: A published Homo Faber interview records Steve Overthrow reporting that he learned partly from Mike Turnock.

nodes.label: Source-family boundary
nodes.text: The THR record explicitly treats two Heritage Crafts pages as one institutional evidence family rather than two independent witnesses.

nodes.label: Tacit transmission gap
nodes.text: What was transmitted, reconstructed, adapted, or newly learned across the revival remains unresolved.

nodes.label: Completeness of survival
nodes.text: Whether all materially important tacit knowledge survived the extinction interval remains unknown.

edges.note: Reported revival establishes renewed practice but does not itself establish continuity of all tacit skill.
A reported direct-learning route narrows the gap but does not establish the content or completeness of transmission.
Treating related institutional pages as one evidence family prevents apparent repetition from becoming extra independent support.
The missing transmission detail blocks a claim that the older tacit skill was preserved completely.
Unknown survival completeness prevents equating revival with full continuity.
